head: 452 of 533
deck: members of Congress have a tie on the public record to Anthropic’s network: 333 through something the network or the member did, 119 only through what third parties did. The network is the company, the funders behind it, the groups they fund, and their PACs and lobbyists.
note: The network, by one chain: Coefficient Giving (then Open Philanthropy) named Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna as its main funders; it awarded Georgetown’s CSET $55.0M in 2019; 19 committee appearances by CSET’s witnesses are on record here. Third parties are lobbyists at the network’s lobbying firms, who gave their own money, and super PACs that received network money and made their own expenditures. A tie can cut either way: a statement may be criticism, and a super PAC may have spent against the member. It is not an allegation, and a contribution is not a vote.
bridge: Start with the company: its employees’ own gifts, and its PAC’s.
how: Each dot is one of the 533 members serving on Nov. 26, 2026. A tie is a public record that links the member and the network: a contribution, a lobbying report on the member’s bill, a fellow in the office, a statement.

head: At the end of 2024, 10 members now serving had received money from Anthropic’s employees or its PAC. By Sept. 30, 2026: 196.
deck: The employees gave their own money: $5.6M, 92% of it dated 2026. The company’s PAC made its first gift on record to a member now serving on June 29, 2026; by Sept. 30 it had given $200K to 81 members, 18 of whom had no gift from an employee.
note: A person’s contribution is their own money, not their employer’s. Employer is as the giver reported it to the FEC. Both counts are of the members serving on Nov. 26, 2026; the record stops at Sept. 30, 2026.
bridge: $5.8M in all. The large money moved another way.
source: Source: FEC contribution records in this project’s tables: contributions to the campaign, leadership PAC or single-member joint fundraising committee of a serving member, through Sept. 30, 2026; ANTHROPAC is Anthropic PBC’s political action committee.

head: Anthropic announced $40.0M for Public First Action. There the trail stops: no filing in this record lists the group’s donors.
deck: FEC receipts show Public First Action gave to 6 committees. The largest candidate total was $15.0M for Alexander Bores, outside Congress, while the committees reported $2.2M against sitting member Seth Moulton.
note: This record traces no contribution to a specific expenditure. A contribution does not direct spending.
bridge: The network’s funders gave more, and for longer.
source: Sources include Anthropic’s announcements and FEC receipt and outside-spending filings.

head: The network’s funders gave more: $170M to outside political groups since 2016, $100M of it from Dustin Moskovitz to Future Forward.
deck: The spending panel covers committees with a network receipt on file and spending that names a serving member.
note: This record traces no gift to a specific expenditure.
bridge: One kind of money reaches more members than any of this, and the network did not give it.
source: Sources include FEC contribution and outside-spending reports, BEMC 4 Association’s IRS filing and Anthropic’s announcements.

head: Lobbyists’ own gifts reach the most members: $1.8M went to campaigns or committees linked to 356 serving members.
note: The gift is the lobbyist’s own money. The record does not say why it was made. Named lobbyists only: $1.3M in 1,022 gifts.
bridge: That is the lobbyists’ own money. Anthropic’s lobbying is on another record.
how: Counted: a gift whose giver was a registered lobbyist at a firm that had a network client in that period. Each lit seat has a campaign or committee linked to a gift.
source: Lobbyists’ semi-annual contribution reports to Congress, Feb. 19, 2021 to June 30, 2026. Filed recipient names, and committee records where the filing gives them, identify the member for each counted gift.

head: Anthropic reported $5.6M in lobbying expenses from January through September 2026.
deck: The company began filing its own expenses in 2024. Outside firms filed the earliest reports in this record.
note: Amounts are as filed, rounded. In quarters with a company report, the totals use its expenses alone.
bridge: Which bills did its reports name?
source: Source: quarterly federal lobbying reports (LD-2) filed by or for Anthropic through Sept. 30, 2026.

head: The three bill families most often named in lobbying reports filed for Anthropic are about chips.
deck: All six sponsors received gifts from Anthropic’s employees or its PAC. How often did a sponsor in the reports receive a gift?
note: A report naming a bill leaves open whether the sponsor’s office was contacted. No filing in this record ties a gift to a bill.
bridge: The gifts and the lobbying are recent. Who was Congress hearing from before them?
source: Sources: quarterly lobbying reports through Sept. 30, 2026, verified sponsors of stand-alone bills and federal contribution filings.

head: By the end of 2024, seven of the network’s funders had awarded $528M in grants, and Congress had heard from seven of their grantees.
deck: By then, ten of the members now serving had received money from Anthropic’s employees or its PAC. The grants supported work on AI, technology, biosecurity and catastrophic risk; none of the grants shown names a member of Congress as its recipient.
note: A grant to an organisation is not money to a member, and an award is not a payment on its date. Testifying is not lobbying.
source: Source: IRS Form 990 grant schedules and the funders’ own published grant lists; witness lists from congress.gov, House committee pages and Senate hearing transcripts.

head: Horizon, a network grantee, has funded 25 fellows inside Congress.
deck: The Horizon Institute for Public Service has $11.9M in network grants on record. Horizon says the host manages a fellow’s work.
note: Horizon also has funders outside the network. A job or a seat is not evidence about the work done in it.
bridge: Grants, hearings, fellows, jobs, money. What does that leave on file for each member?
source: Source: Horizon Institute placement pages and alumni lists, and its “Host a Fellow” page as saved in 2026; House and Senate payroll reports, lobbyists’ disclosed former posts and organisations’ staff pages; IRS Form 990 grant schedules; for the sheet, FEC contribution records through Sept. 30, 2026.

head: A record of ties, not a record of influence.
deck: 240 of the 452 members with a tie have one or two kinds of record. The opening slide’s two members again, with what is on file for each: seven kinds of record for Ted Lieu, one for Thom Tillis.
how: Each dot is one of the 533 members serving on Nov. 26, 2026, by party; records through Sept. 30, 2026.
